# `start`

A way a game can begin, until game scenarios exist: a realm, where the character begins and the template it is made from by default (12 §3.4).

## Fields

Besides these, a definition takes the [keys every definition carries](README.md#keys-every-definition-carries).

- `name` (string; optional): What the start is called where the player chooses one. Left out, its id.
- `doc` (string; optional): A line or two about it.
- `realm` (string; **required**): The realm definition the game's world is made from: a qualified id, or a bare name, which means the realm of that name in the start's own namespace.
- `at` (list of whole number; **required**): Where the character begins, in cells of the realm's base grid: `[x, y]`, which means the highest cell of that column a walker can stand in, or `[x, y, z]`, which means exactly that cell.
- `template` (string, or `null`; optional): The `template` the player's character is made from, with every choice at its default, when the player has made no character of their own (06 §10): a qualified id, or a bare name in the start's own namespace. Left out, a game can begin here only with a character the player made.
- `glyph` (object [`GlyphDef`](#glyphdef), or `null`; optional): How the player's character is drawn when none of its templates gives a glyph. Left out, such a character is drawn as the theme's text.
- `senses` (list of string; optional): The senses the player's character perceives with when its templates give it none (15 §4): `sense` definitions by qualified id, or bare names in the start's own namespace. Left out, every sense the loaded mods define.
- `saving` (string, or `null`; optional): The saving policy of the game (13 §9.2): `free` (save and load at will, the default), `single` (one save, written on leaving), `checkpoints` (only the saves rules make) or `none`.

<a id="glyphdef"></a>
### `GlyphDef`

A `glyph` as a definition writes it (12 §4.1).

- `ch` (one character, or `null`; optional): The character: one Unicode character of single width. Required unless `shape` is given.
- `fg` (string, or `null`; optional): The colour of the character: a colour name, `#rrggbb`, `"material"`, `"own"` or `"dress"`. Left out, the theme's text colour.
- `bg` (string, or `null`; optional): The colour behind the character, written like `fg`. `null` or left out: whatever is beneath.
- `bold` (`true` or `false`, or `null`; optional): Whether the character is drawn bold.
- `by_state` (object, name → object [`GlyphPartDef`](#glyphpartdef); optional): Parts replaced while the element is in a named state.
- `by_level` (list of object [`GlyphPartDef`](#glyphpartdef); optional): Parts replaced by field or damage level: entry 0 for level 0, and so on. A level past the end uses the last entry.
- `shape` (object, one of `"north"`, `"east"`, `"south"`, `"west"` ([`Facing`](#facing)) → list of string; optional): For a thing that fills several cells: rows of characters, one per cell of its footprint, for a facing. Facings not given are turned from the first one that is.
- `layer` (whole number; optional): Drawn over (positive) or under (negative) its usual place in the order of 12 §6.1.

<a id="glyphpartdef"></a>
### `GlyphPartDef`

The parts of a glyph that a state, a level or a look can replace.

- `ch` (one character, or `null`; optional): The character: one Unicode character of single width.
- `fg` (string, or `null`; optional): The colour of the character.
- `bg` (string, or `null`; optional): The colour behind it. `null` or left out: whatever is beneath.
- `bold` (`true` or `false`, or `null`; optional): Whether the character is drawn bold.

<a id="facing"></a>
### `Facing`

A direction a thing of several cells can face.

One of:

- `"north"`: Toward the top of the map.
- `"east"`: Toward the right.
- `"south"`: Toward the bottom.
- `"west"`: Toward the left.
